newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai state oil firm says falling baht hikes costs.
newsitem.headline: Thai state oil firm says falling baht hikes costs.

text.p: The sliding baht will soon push up pump prices further for consumers, the top executive at state-run Petroleum Authority of Thailand said on Wednesday.
Pala Sookawesh, PTT chairman, told reporters that as the baht broke the 31.00 level, the cost of retail oil prices would rise by 60 satangs per litre.
The baht hit a record low of 32.60 against the dollar on Wednesday, sparking central bank intervention, dealers said.
But so far the company, which has the biggest market share in retail oil business, has only raised its prices by 15 satangs per litre since the baht was floated on July 2.
Pala declined to say when PTT would adjust pump prices again but said it would try to shoulder the burden as long as possible.
"We will try our best to delay passing the cost to consumers to help government maintain price stability. But I don't know how long we can do that," he said.
